LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.1: Reading Aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Aloud, part of Reading in Grade 4 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How can you pronounce words clearly when reading aloud?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read out the syllables and words correctly then outline initials and finals used respectively,

2. work together to combine jumbled up initials, finals and tones to form correct Chinese syllables and words,

3. read short passages on basic greetings and self-introduction aloud (hello & one’s name i.e. nǐ/nín hǎo, wǒ jiào ...... nǐ ne?),

4. take turns reading short passages on self-introduction aloud with peers,

5. practice reading out rhymes on similar words with different tones in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read out the syllables and words correctly then outline initials and finals used respectively,
2. work together to combine jumbled up initials, finals and tones to form correct Chinese syllables and words,
3. read short passages on basic greetings and self-introduction aloud (hello & one’s name i.e. nǐ/nín hǎo, wǒ jiào ...... nǐ ne?),
4. take turns reading short passages on self-introduction aloud with peers,
5. practice reading out rhymes on similar words with different tones in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner works collaboratively with peers to form correct Chinese syllables and

words.

Values:
Respect: The learner displays patience as they wait for their turn to read short passages on self-introduction.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Intercultural awareness: The learner becomes aware of cultural differences in greetings that exist between their own languages

and Chinese when they read short passages on introduction.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner links their learning to English and Kiswahili on the importance of correct pronunciation of sounds and words in

communication.
